title: What Kind of Professional Will You Be?
description:
After about a year on the job — things have started to come into focus.

There were two ways to move up in this company.
Prove your worth in numbers.
Or rise through people.

There were people who knew both paths.
{name} thought today about which one to take.

choices.text: Prove it with results — because numbers don't lie  [Elite Track]
choices.result_text:
{name} reopened the report.
At a desk everyone else had already left, he polished the numbers.
This way is lonely. But the results are hard to argue with.
That's what {name} decided to lean on.

choices.text: Rise through people — because in this world, it always comes back to people  [Social Climber]
choices.result_text:
{name} bought his team lead lunch first.
He became the person who picks up the phone before the calculator does.
There are things numbers alone can't cover —
he was starting to learn that in his gut.

title: How Will You Make Money Work for You?
description:
After a few wins and a few losses — a style of his own had started to form.

Some investors believe in spreadsheets.
Expected value, standard deviation, correlation.
People who wield the emotionlessness of numbers as a weapon.

Some investors believe in instinct.
People who look for when the market is wrong — and bet big.

Which way fits {name}?

choices.text: Fight with data and probability — stripping out emotion is the edge  [Quant]
choices.result_text:
From that day on, {name} started building spreadsheets.
Every position, laid out in numbers.
He was wrong sometimes. But he didn't get shaken.
That was the power of this approach.

choices.text: When conviction comes, bet big — being timid kills compounding  [Speculator]
choices.result_text:
{name} put in twice as much as usual on a single position.
If he was wrong, it was over.
He was right.
After that day, {name} decided to trust this instinct.

title: What Will You Build?
description:
People who dream of founding a startup come in two kinds.

The kind who want to turn an idea into a product.
People who start from the question: 'Why doesn't this exist?'

The kind who want to gather people.
People who start from: 'Something will happen if these people come together.'

Which one is {name}?

choices.text: Build something nobody else has — product comes first  [Tech Founder]
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote the first outline in his notebook.
He asked not 'can it be built' but 'should it be built' first.
Technology is just a tool. If the problem is real, the tool will follow.
That was the way {name} believed in.

choices.text: Build a place where people gather — the network is the asset  [Social Entrepreneur]
choices.result_text:
{name} had his business cards remade.
An era where the contact matters more than the title.
One person brings two, two bring four.
{name} decided to be the starting point.

title: The Day the Numbers Speak
description:
Quarterly report presentation day.

{name}'s materials were different. In a room full of other teams' 'vibes' and 'directions,'
{name} spoke only in numbers. Conversion rates, cost efficiency, six-month trends.

Afterwards, the team lead called him aside.
"How did you put this together? Your data sources are different."

Not a criticism. Recognition.
A lonely road. But the numbers didn't lie.

choices.text: Accept the recognition — this is my method
choices.result_text:
The team lead cited {name}'s materials in the next quarter's presentation.
It was a quiet way to rise.
Not flashy — but hard to argue with.
That was the nature of the weapon {name} had chosen.

choices.text: But also know that you walked it alone — this loneliness was my choice too
choices.result_text:
At the team dinner, {name} sat a little apart.
Recognized for results, but a bit more distance from the people around him.
The good and the bad — both part of the method he'd chosen.
{name} kept walking this path, knowing that.

title: The Door People Open
description:
The team lead pulled {name} aside.
"There's a spot opening up in the HQ task force next month.
If I put your name in from our side, you can get in."

The relationships {name} had built bore fruit — not through numbers, but another way.
It wasn't recognition first. It was trust first.
He'd learned that when trust accumulates, opportunity finds you.

But on the other hand — he also knew that a colleague with better results had been passed over.

choices.text: Take the opportunity — this is what my method looks like when it pays off
choices.result_text:
He joined the task force. The colleague's name never came up.
For the first time, {name} looked squarely at the fact
that the road to Gangnam has moments that aren't clean.

choices.text: That colleague is sitting on his mind — is this really the right way
choices.result_text:
He thought about it for a long time. In the end, he joined anyway.
But he bought that colleague lunch. Without saying anything.
As long as he kept rising this way — he'd decided to carry at least that much debt.

title: The Day the Model Was Right
description:
The market crashed.

Everyone panic-selling. Social media flooded with 'it's over.'

{name} opened the spreadsheet.
The numbers said — oversold territory. Expected value positive. Entry timing.

His hands were shaking. Emotion made him doubt the model.
But {name} knew: this was where the real test of the quant approach began.

choices.text: Follow the model — trust the numbers, not the feeling
choices.result_text:
He took the position. Three weeks later the market bounced back.
He'd bought when everyone else was selling.
The model was right. But he also understood how hard it was to actually pull the trigger knowing that.
The quant's real competitor isn't the market — it's yourself.

choices.text: The model might be wrong this time — hold off for now
choices.result_text:
The market bounced back. {name}'s model had been right.
But without trust in it, he'd missed the call.
Next time — the person who built the model would trust the model.

title: What Conviction Is Worth
description:
{name} had been watching for a long time.
A sector he'd spotted himself. A stock no one else was paying attention to.
He'd read in his gut that institutions were accumulating.

And today, he went in big.
Double the usual position size.

Two hours later, major news hit that stock.
The price climbed 30%.

If he'd been wrong, it would have been over. He was right.
The speculator's finest moment.

choices.text: Take the profit — my gut called it right
choices.result_text:
Sold. The gain landed in the account.
This instinct isn't always right. But today it was.
The real question — how he'd handle this instinct when it's wrong —
{name} didn't yet know.

choices.text: Stay in — the ceiling isn't here yet
choices.result_text:
It went up more. Then pulled back.
He cut at -15% from the top.
Still a profit. But he could have made more.
The speculator is fated to walk forever between greed and restraint.

title: First User
description:
Months of building.
Something that might never get used.

Then today, a notification.
The first real user.

A stranger had sought out what {name} had made and was using it.
"This helped me." One line.

This one line was the first confirmation of what {name} had been enduring these months to reach.

choices.text: Reach out directly — I want to know more
choices.result_text:
A reply came back. Pain points, wants, reasons for using it.
Directions {name} hadn't thought of.
The product's direction isn't decided by the person who builds it — it's the person who uses it.
One person's feedback taught him that.

choices.text: Put your head down and build the next version
choices.result_text:
Grateful. But now there was work to do.
{name} opened his notebook and started writing down the next version's list.
If one person uses it, ten can.
If ten use it, a hundred can.

title: Compound Interest on Connection
description:
Something strange happened.

Person A, met six months ago, introduced {name} to person B.
B told C, and C told D.

D reached out.
"Do you know Minjun? I'd like to talk about possibly working together."

{name} had never met D. But D already knew {name}.
This was the moment the network had started moving on its own.

choices.text: Set up the meeting with D — this is how network compounding works
choices.result_text:
He had coffee with D. Around D were E and F.
{name} handed out five business cards.
At first, meeting people had been an investment.
Now that investment was growing on its own.

choices.text: Pause and ask — is all of this genuine
choices.result_text:
He thought about it. How many in this network were actually sincere.
Probably not half.
But if half are genuine, that's enough.
{name} sent D a reply.
